# The Bearish Case for Oil and Gold with Queen Anne's Gate Capital

First listed: 2026-07-08 | Evaluation cutoff: 2026-11-10

[Back to library](../README.md)

## Source versions

- [Substack: The Bearish Case for Oil and Gold with Queen Anne's Gate Capital](https://realeismanplaybook.substack.com/p/the-bearish-case-for-oil-and-gold) - 2026-07-08

Earliest listed publication among matched versions, not proof of an unedited contemporaneous archive. Claim timestamps refer to the reviewed version.

## Summary

Kathleen Kelley argues that war-driven demand destruction and new supply will create severe oil surpluses, potentially pushing prices into the twenties. Nancy O'Flynn sees crowded gold positioning and prefers silver. Eisman mostly reports their views, adding conditional consumer and equity implications plus a separate critique of crypto. Chinese refinery weakness and delayed reserve replenishment have support. However, contemporaneous Gulf supply shortfalls and falling onshore stocks contradict assertions of fully offset disruption. Long-run oil balances remain future-dated, while renewed central-bank gold buying weakens the proposed demand-exhaustion mechanism.

The central oil forecast is conditional on restored flows and extends beyond the cutoff. Current physical-balance claims deserve different verdicts from that future scenario. Eisman does not unconditionally adopt the guest $20 oil target; his closing $40-50 framing is his interpretation, not a second explicit guest target.

## Framework and tools

- Build commodity balances from supply, consumption, trade and inventories.
- Separate final consumption from stockpiling and refinery demand.
- Distinguish crude availability from refined-product bottlenecks.
- Test geopolitical narratives against routes, capacity and realized output.
- Separate positioning, prices and causal explanations.
- Preserve conditional forecasts and the time required for retail price pass-through.

Tools and charts discussed, not a complete visual inspection:

- Country production and refinery runs
- China imports and stockpiles
- Oil supply-demand balances for 2027-2028
- Saudi and UAE pipeline capacity
- Strategic reserve release and refill schedules
- Gold ETF flows and commitments of traders
- Central-bank reserve purchases
- Silver industrial and jewelry demand
- Oil price moving averages and inflation lags
- Crypto-Nasdaq correlation

## Source cautions

SPEAKER_00 is Steve Eisman, SPEAKER_02 is Kathleen Kelley and SPEAKER_01 is Nancy O'Flynn, established by named introductions, backgrounds and the explicit handoff to Nancy near 1545 seconds. The publisher captions spell Kelley as Kelly; attribution uses the identified Queen Anne's Gate economist.
- Publication is July 8; an exact recording date is not stated. References to a ceasefire and oil in the seventies locate a particular interim market regime.
- Kelley and O'Flynn spellings are normalized; speaker assignments are supported by introductions.
- A Saudi export statement combines inconsistent component totals; do not silently reconcile them.
- Demand is sometimes used for refinery demand, final consumption and apparent demand interchangeably.
- The closing recap says oil where context clearly means gold.
- Nancy locates $5,200 in early 2026; Eisman later incorrectly places it at 2025 year-end.
- The closing $40-50 oil base-case suggestion is Eisman interpretation; Kelley explicitly discusses possible twenties.
